sovereign_country.strategic_role: 西欧核心消费市场、高客单价品牌合规与本土清关

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Foreign Market Feasibility Study and Regulatory Licensing Agency

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: France–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (renegotiated on 26 November 2007; effective 20 August 2010)
France–China Double Taxation Avoidance Convention (signed 30 May 1984; effective 1 January 1987; amended by Protocol signed 26 November 2013)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Articles L. 561-1 to L. 561-49 of the French Monetary and Financial Code (Code monétaire et financier), as amended by Loi n° 2020-1023 of 10 August 2020 and Ordonnance n° 2020-115 of 12 February 2020; Articles L. 561-45 to L. 561-46 and R. 561-54 of the same code; Articles R. 123-220 to R. 123-224 of the French Commercial Code (Code de commerce) establishing the beneficial-owner declaration in the Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Existence Certificate of each corporate shareholder (Extrait de registre des sociétés du pays d'origine)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Original company registry of the shareholder's country of incorporation (e.g., Companies House, ACRA, Hong Kong Companies Registry)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if country of origin is a Hague Convention member) OR Consular Legalization through the French Embassy/Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (Pouvoir) appointing the French-resident representative for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction where the power is granted
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (required for signature outside France) or Consular Legalization; sworn French translation mandatory

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity document (passport/national ID) of all ultimate beneficial owners and proposed managers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority of the document holder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified true copy plus sworn French translation; apostille/consular legalization may be required for certain high-risk jurisdictions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, beneficial owners, directors and authorised representatives against (i) the UN Security Council Consolidated Sanctions List; (ii) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List; (iii) the French national asset-freezing list (Gels d'avoirs) maintained by the Direction générale du Trésor; (iv) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN) List; and (v) reliable PEP databases covering national and foreign PEPs (including EU Directive 2015/849 definitions). Negative results must be documented; positive or ambiguous hits require escalation to the firm's MLRO/Compliance Officer and may result in refusal of engagement or enhanced due diligence (EDD).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Guichet unique des formalités des entreprises — formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr (official French one-stop shop operated by ANTS for company incorporation); name availability reference via Infogreffe and INPI databases.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Latin characters; if a foreign-script name is intended, a transliteration into French must be provided and used in all statutory filings. The name must be distinctive and not contrary to public order or good morals. The suffix 'SARL' or 'Société à responsabilité limitée' must be included. Non-French names are accepted provided they are Latin-script and not misleading.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Notaire, Avocat, Médecin, Pharmacie (regulated professions, protected title)
République, État, France (state/sovereignty connotation; prior ministerial consent required)
Région, Département, Commune (territorial collectivity protected names)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Although France does not operate a statutory name-reservation system, the clearance certificate obtained from the registry/INPI is treated as valid for a 30-day working window. If the registry (greffe) refuses the name, the applicant may (i) request written reasons from the greffe; (ii) submit an appeal to the judge responsible for supervision of the register (juge commis à la surveillance du registre) within fifteen (15) days of the refusal; (iii) file an altered name application for immediate reconsideration; or (iv) where the refusal is based on third-party rights, obtain a formal letter of consent/waiver from the right holder or initiate proceedings before the Tribunal judiciaire. This SOP also permits contact with the INPI for trademark-clearing before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a market-entry consultancy: French law (Article L. 123-11-1 of the Commercial Code) allows registration at the offices of an authorised domiciliation company, provided a formal domiciliation agreement is concluded and a physical contactable location is maintained during office hours. Purely 'letterbox' arrangements without any correspondence service are not acceptable; a revitalised office may increase tax/VAT substance scrutiny but remains lawful for this industry.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low risk for an unregulated consultancy: approximately 1%–3% annualised probability of an unannounced inspection under normal conditions; probability rises sharply to greater than 25% if the register office is a mail-drop only, if turnover is artificially shifted, or if red flags are triggered by bank or AML monitoring.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Name clearance and availability search (INPI/Infogreffe combined) — corporate law firm fee
Sworn legal translation of foreign corporate shareholder documents (traduction assermentée)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Sworn translator (traducteur assermenté) listed with French appeal courts

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization and apostille/consular legalisation of Power of Attorney and identity documents (where foreign signatures are needed)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notary / competent foreign authority and French consular post if applicable
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official consular fee schedule plus notary tariff

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Preparation of French articles of association (statuts) for SARL (including legal review of capital and shareholder provisions)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: French corporate attorney / certified notaire (if deed notarised)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market rate for SARL incorporation (€800–€1,500)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Mandatory legal notice (annonce légale) in an authorised French legal gazette
French corporate registry filing fee (Guichet unique: FBE and RCS registration)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Greffe du tribunal de commerce (commercial court registry)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official fixed tariff (frais de greffe), approximately €40–€100

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO register preparation and KYC/AML sanctions screening (PEP, UN, OFAC, EU, French list) for all UBOs and managers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance/KYC provider (law firm or specialist firm)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company bank account opening assistance (Wise B2B, Banque de France listed institutions) and share capital deposit support
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Bank or payment institution plus intermediary
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Bank published fee schedule and service fee

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Book II, Articles L.223-1 through L.223-43 (formation, contributions, and management of the Societe a Responsabilite Limitee)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the judicial district of the registered office; electronic filing portal operated by Infogreffe (www.infogreffe.fr) in liaison with the Centre de Formalites des Entreprises (CFE)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (Articles of Association) accompanied by the M0 creation declaration (Cerfa No. 16526), the bank capital deposit certificate, and the constitutive legal announcement publication attestation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for SARL (may be set at EUR 1); where capital is set, cash contributions must be released at least to 20% at formation and the unpaid balance within 5 years; subscription and released funds are held in escrow by a licensed French bank or the Caisse des Depots et Consignations until registration is completed
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved by the founding members of the SARL at the First Board Meeting that: (1) The share capital of EUR 1,000 is subscribed in full, with cash contributions released at the statutory minimum and held in escrow with a licensed French bank per Article L.223-7 of the French Commercial Code; (2) The registered office is established at the address stated in the Articles of Association, France; (3) [Name] is appointed Gerant (Manager) for an indefinite term with full power to represent the Company; (4) The Gerant is authorized to open bank accounts, publish the legal announcement, and file the incorporation dossier with the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft, Execute and Optionally Notarize the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Private deed (sous seing prive) prepared with legal counsel or executed before a Notaire (notary) where notarization is elected; eIDAS-certified electronic signature is admissible
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare French-language statuts stating the corporate form (SARL), corporate object limited to consultancy, registered office address, share capital and cash contributions, management powers, and decision-making rules; have each founding member sign the final page with the mention 'lu et approuve'; where in-kind contributions exceed EUR 30,000 or carry special advantages, obtain a statutory auditor (commissaire aux apports) valuation report and annex it to the statuts.
required_dossiers: Valid government-issued passport or national ID of each founding member
Proof of residential or professional address (e.g., utility bill or lease)
Draft statuts in French language
Commissaire aux apports valuation report (only if in-kind contributions exceed EUR 30,000)
Declaration of no criminal convictions (declaration de non-condamnation) for each proposed Gerant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry identifies defects in the statuts (missing clauses, imprecise corporate object, irregular contribution provisions), execute a corrective deed (acte rectificatif) signed by all members and re-file the corrected instrument.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit Paid-Up Share Capital in an Escrow Bank Account
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed French credit institution or the Caisse des Depots et Consignations (CDC) receiving the capital deposit (depot des fonds)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a provisional account in the name of the SARL en formation; deposit cash contributions representing at least 20% of the subscribed capital; obtain the bank's capital deposit certificate (attestation de depot des fonds), which is indispensable to the registration filing; the funds remain blocked until presentation of the registry certificate (extrait Kbis) proving legal existence.
required_dossiers: Signed draft statuts
Bank account opening and deposit application form
Identity documents of the contributing members
Mandate designating the legal representative empowered to block and later release the funds
List of subscribers with their capital allocations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses account opening on KYC/AML grounds, invoke the right to an account (droit au compte) through the Banque de France, which designates a depositary institution within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved legal announcements journal (Journal d'Annonces Legales) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the constitutive announcement text to the approved JAL stating the corporate form, company name, share capital, registered office, corporate object, total contributions, the Gerant, and the commercial registry where the company will be registered; secure the publication attestation (attestation de parution); ensure the attestation is not older than one month at the time of the registry filing.
required_dossiers: Text of the constitutive legal announcement
Extract of the statuts summarizing the required legal particulars
Power of attorney to the publisher if submitted by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the announcement contains inaccuracies, publish a corrective announcement (avis rectificatif) in the same JAL and provide both the original and correction attestations; if the publication becomes stale (over one month old) before filing, re-publish the announcement.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File the Incorporation Dossier with the Commercial Court Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the district of the registered office; electronic filing via www.infogreffe.fr or alternatively through the CFE
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Assemble the complete dossier (statuts, capital deposit certificate, legal announcement attestation, M0 creation form, manager consent and non-condemnation declarations) and file online through the Infogreffe procedural interface; pay the applicable registry and ancillary state fees electronically; the registry must process the application within 5 working days and issue a certificate of filing upon acceptance; the company acquires legal personality on registration in the Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS).
required_dossiers: Signed statuts (original plus examination copy)
Bank capital deposit certificate (attestation de depot des fonds)
Legal announcement attestation (attestation de parution)
M0 creation declaration form (Cerfa No. 16526*04)
Manager consent and declaration of non-condemnation
Power of attorney if filed through a corporate service provider
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registry issues a rejection notice (rejet) listing irregularities, cure each point and re-file within the prescribed delay; demonstrate that all procedural defects have been rectified; in case of registry inertia, escalate by formal letter to the greffier or petition the supervising judge (juge charge des greffes).

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the Registration Certificate and Extrait Kbis
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (registry back-office)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the dossier, the registry assigns the SIREN number, SIRET establishment number, and the NAF/APE activity code; the company is inscribed in the Registre du Commerce et des Societes and the extrait Kbis is issued as the official proof of legal existence; request the Kbis through the Infogreffe online account and verify the accuracy of the registered corporate data.
required_dossiers: None for ordinary issuance - the Kbis is delivered ex officio after registration; supplementary evidence only if rectification of registered data is requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Kbis is delayed beyond the statutory timeframe, file a written reminder to the registry; if the registered data are erroneous, submit a request for rectification (demande de rectification) with supporting documents; in the event of serious registry inaction, petition the supervising judges for a compliance order.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable - ISIC 7020 overseas market entry consultancy is a non-industrial tertiary activity; no industrial licensing board jurisdiction is triggered for standard office-based consultancy operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required - the activity does not require an industrial operating permit under French licensing rules; ordinary RCS registration evidenced by the extrait Kbis and, where premises are leased, a valid bail commercial suffice

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministere de la Transition Ecologique / DREAL (Direction Regionale de l'Environnement, de l'Amenagement et du Logement)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - tertiary service activity outside the scope of ICPE (Installations Classees pour la Protection de l'Environnement) registration; no environmental impact assessment report required for office-based consulting services
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Zero regulated industrial effluent or VOC emissions at source; office-generated waste, paper, and packaging are subject to municipal waste collection bylaws and the extended producer responsibility schemes where applicable; office premises above 1,000 m2 fall within the tertiary sector energy reduction decree (decret tertiaire) annual reporting obligations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Office workplace compliance under the Code du travail (Articles R.4223-1 et seq.): fire safety checks, electrical installation conformity inspection, emergency evacuation signage and drills; where clients are received, ERP (Type X) fire safety certification issued by the Commission de Securite; structural load and building maintenance certificates supplied by the lessor under the bail commercial; personnel registration with URSSAF and workplace health and safety documentation with the CSE where applicable.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Direction Générale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via the official portal at https://www.impots.gouv.fr/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned entities operating as SARL in France must register with the DGFiP to obtain a SIREN number. Non-resident owners may appoint a French tax representative. Registration involves filing Form 1388-A or equivalent for VAT purposes, providing corporate documents, and obtaining approval. The SIREN serves as the unique tax identifier for corporate and VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections available. However, the micro-entreprise regime is available for small businesses under specific turnover thresholds and conditions. France adheres to OECD BEPS guidelines for addressing hybrid mismatches through domestic legislation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (TVA - Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: 85,000 EUR annual turnover threshold for VAT registration in most cases; reduced thresholds may apply for intra-Community supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing (facturation électronique) for all B2B transactions since October 2024, requiring real-time transmission of invoice data to the French tax authorities through certified platforms or APIs, with digital time-stamping (horodatage fiscal) mandatory.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT rate applies to exports of goods from France and to services performed outside France and invoiced to non-French customers. Eligibility requires verifiable proof of export or performance abroad, including customs documentation for goods and evidence of service delivery and payment for services.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Déclaration en Douane d'Exportation - DAU)
Bill of Lading or equivalent transport document
Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificat de Règlement Intérieur) confirming receipt of payment from abroad
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims of zero-rating must be substantiated; fraudulent or unsubstantiated claims may lead to penalties of 40% of the VAT due, interest surcharges, and potential criminal liability. Retrospective adjustments and clawbacks apply upon audit if documentation is insufficient.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France, in coordination with the Direction Générale du Trésor (French Treasury) and the European Central Bank, administers foreign exchange policy and maintains the monetary and macro-prudential framework for euro-area operations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France offers full current and capital account convertibility under the eurosystem framework and OECD liberalisation commitments. A French SARL may receive foreign currency proceeds, hold multi-currency accounts, and remit dividends to non-resident shareholders without prior exchange-control approval. Dividend remittance to non-EU shareholders may attract withholding tax unless reduced or eliminated by the relevant double taxation treaty or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive. No exchange control barriers apply to trade-related current payments or funding flows relating to market-entry consultancy contracts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory surrender requirement or mandatory conversion ratio exists for French export receipts. Export proceeds may be retained in EUR or foreign currency at a French-authorised credit institution without any minimum repatriation timetable. For accounting and tax reporting, foreign currency balances are converted to EUR at the applicable period-end exchange rate under French GAAP and IFRS rules; for balance-of-payments statistics, the receiving bank must report certain euro-area and non-euro-area flows to the Banque de France.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with EUR and USD multi-currency capabilities

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Moderate for auxiliary cross-border disbursement and FX conversion; Low for primary operating account and capital escrow functions. Legal constraint: an offshore EMI must hold a valid e-money institution licence or passport through the European Economic Area under the Second Payment Services Directive (PSD2) to provide payment services to a French SARL without triggering unauthorised activity. Non-EEA EMIs without a French/EEA licence cannot lawfully offer commercial account services in France and should be avoided for treasury-critical flows.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A French SARL with non-resident directors may undergo remote KYC onboarding using a video interview, an apostilled notarised resolution, a certified copy of the passport of each significant beneficial owner, and a French commercial registry extract (extrait Kbis). Most French banks reserve the right to request a physical meeting at the relationship branch where the beneficial owner is a politically exposed person or where an enhanced due-diligence trigger applies; however, physical presence is not a statutory universal mandate for low-risk market-entry consultants.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Newly incorporated SARL with zero operating history and a foreign parent making a lump-sum paid-in capital injection.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Extrait Kbis; notarised shares subscription certificate; board resolution approving the capital increase; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds letter; projected cash-flow statement evidencing consultancy contract pipeline.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner residing in a FATF-monitored or embargoed jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passport copies; internationally recognised third-party KYC compliance certificate; positive adverse-media assessment; local bank reference letter; proof of at least 12 months of lawful professional activity unrelated to sanctions.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Transactions comprising high-value margin payments or third-party settlement requests inconsistent with advisory fee patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed master services agreement; client trust account statement; per-invoice delivery acceptance records; explanation of the specific market-entry milestone triggering each payment; bank reference from the originating institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Request to create a Capital Escrow Account available for onward distribution to foreign sub-agents.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Interparty escrow agreement; detailed sub-agent commissioning schedule; identity documents of all downstream recipients; French tax advisor opinion confirming no unlawful lending or deposit-taking activity in applying the monies.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Route inbound paid-in capital or funds to the SARL by using an SWIFT MT103 for non-SEPA transactions or a SEPA credit transfer for euro-denominated payments, inserting in the remittance information field the phrase SHARE CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION or CURRENT ACCOUNT ADVANCE together with the relevant shareholders resolution reference and the French SIREN number. If the injection constitutes direct investment as defined by French balance-of-payments rules, the reporting obligation is discharged through the bank and the transaction purpose code must be completed in accordance with the Banque de France balance-of-payments and international investment-position reporting framework.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: use a SEPA Credit Transfer for euro payments within the Single Euro Payments Area; use SWIFT MT103/COV for high-value or non-EU cross-currency commercial payments; use MT700/707 series for documentary letters of credit where trade finance and documentary compliance are required. For urgent structural transactions, rely on TARGET2 eligible ancillary systems operated through the Banque de France. All outbound wires must include the purpose code identifying the underlying market-entry advisory service and the VAT or tax reference of the supplier.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright deliverable FX forwards in EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CHF with maturities typically up to 12 months, documented by an ISDA 2002 Master Agreement or a domestic French master agreement with a bank counterparty authorised by the ACPR.
FX swaps for temporary conversion of EUR into a settlement currency, executed with a bank treasury desk and collateral governed by the applicable Credit Support Annex.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for exotic or non-convertible currencies referenced against the Reuters or WM/Refinitiv benchmark, using ISDA 2006 FX Definitions and the standard confirmation precedent for the relevant jurisdiction.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps for medium-term debt or revenue exposure, limited to eligible financial counterparties or commercial counterparties transacting under the exemption for non-financial entities hedging commercial risk.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registry (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000 and administrative strike-off after 3 months of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Revenue Service (Direction Générale des Finances Publiques)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 15th day of the 4th month following financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 40% penalty on unpaid tax plus interest and potential strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: French Beneficial Ownership Register (Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually or upon material shareholding changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to €10,000 for non-compliance with beneficial ownership disclosure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory statutory audit if turnover exceeds €800,000 or balance sheet total exceeds €400,000 or number of employees exceeds 50

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual confirmation of UBO details and maintenance of shareholding register for compliance with French beneficial ownership transparency rules

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 50-300 USD annually for registered office and local agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 800-2,500 USD for mandatory certified audit of small SARL

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). Reduced rate of 15% applies to the first EUR 42,500 of taxable profit for qualifying small companies with turnover below EUR 10 million and 25%+ individual ownership.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million and 5% above; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% for eligible innovation expenses up to EUR 400,000; Jeune Entreprise Innovante (JEI) scheme provides up to 100% CIT exemption for the first 7 years on profits capped at EUR 200,000 per year; patent box regime taxes qualifying IP income at 10%; EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may provide 0% tax on qualifying dividend receipts.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_regime_note: France does not apply a strict 5-year cap; net operating losses may be carried forward indefinitely, but the annual offset is limited to EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable profit above that amount. An optional 3-year carryback of up to EUR 1,000,000 is also available. The numeric field reflects the most common statutory reporting cycle for loss schedules in the French liasses fiscales.
corporate_income_tax_regime.ancillary_cit_payment_schedule: CIT is paid in advance via four instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, followed by a final balance settlement within 3 months of the fiscal year-end.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Cerfa n° 2065 (Déclaration de Résultats souscrits) and accompanying liasses fiscales (2050-2054 series). Filed electronically through EDI-TDFC on impots.gouv.fr or via approved EDI partner platforms.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; the SARL must also pay four CIT prepayments on 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December, with the final balance due on the annual filing deadline.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 3 months of the fiscal year-end. For calendar-year taxpayers the usual deadline is 3 May, shifted to the next business day if 3 May falls on a weekend or French public holiday.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Select 'Bénéfice réel' and state whether the small-business reduced rate (15%) or standard rate (25%) applies. Indicate any affiliation with an Article 209 AH tax group or EU parent-subsidiary directive claim.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete this block from the SARL itself even when 100% foreign-owned. If the SARL is owned by an EU parent company, provide the parent's EU tax identification for withholding relief on upstream dividends.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CERFA 2050, Box A/B — Bilan Actif / Passif
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total gross fixed assets, accumulated depreciation, inventory, receivables, cash, shareholder loans and liabilities in accordance with French GAAP (Plan Comptable Général).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure shareholder loans from non-resident directors or parent companies are accurately booked with arm's-length interest rates and recorded in the balance sheet; undocumented current-account balances may be recharacterised as deemed distributions.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Insert the net accounting profit or loss before tax taken from the statutory income statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No translation is required inside the e-filing portal, but the underlying accounting records and signed French GAAP financial statements must be maintained and available for audit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report non-deductible expense add-backs and tax-deductible subtractions such as CIR, CII, patent box deductions and carried-forward losses used in the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Add-back items typically include 50% of passenger vehicle operating leases, fines, excessive directors' remuneration, and management fees paid to a foreign related party without supporting transfer-pricing documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: CERFA 2065, Box R — Résultat fiscal (bénéfice ou déficit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final taxable amount after all adjustments. Apply the 15% reduced rate to the qualifying EUR 42,500 slice and 25% to the remainder; add the 3% surcharge only where taxable turnover exceeds EUR 250 million.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the result is a tax loss, enter it as a negative figure and attach the loss-carryforward schedule. A net loss in a newly established French market-entry or consultancy entity will trigger heightened substance review by the tax administration.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without prior notice: 10% of underlying CIT. Bad-faith filing: 40%. Fraudulent filing or organised tax evasion: 80%. Interest for late payment accrues at 0.20% per month on unpaid balances. Failure to submit balance sheet and statutory accounts to the Companies Registry within 6 months of filing can also lead to administrative fines and a director's travel ban under commercial law.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 30% statutory dividend withholding rate (prélèvement forfaitaire unique equivalent) for non-resident shareholders, unless reduced by an applicable DTA. The EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive can reduce this to 0% for a qualifying corporate parent holding at least 10% of the SARL's capital for 24 consecutive months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: 1) Identify the applicable DTA between France and the recipient's tax residence. 2) Obtain an original Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from the foreign revenue authority, issued within the last 6 months. 3) Submit the TRC, a certificate of beneficial ownership, and any treaty-specific declaration to the French paying SARL before dividend distribution. 4) Apply the reduced rate at source, or if the 30% withholding has been applied, file a reimbursement claim with the French tax office under the general réclamation procedure, no later than 31 December of the second year following the distribution. All supporting documents must be held in the SARL's tax file for a 6-year audit window.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: French domestic source rules apply where a French payer compensates a non-resident recipient. Interest paid to a non-resident is generally subject to 25% withholding under CGI Article 125 A, with treaty relief commonly reducing or abolishing the rate to 0%. Royalties and IP licence fees paid outside France are subject to a domestic withholding rate in the 33.33% zone under the general non-resident income provisions, while applicable DTAs frequently cap royalty withholding at 0% to 10%, and the France-US and many modern European treaties fix interest at 0%. Exact statutory and treaty rates must be confirmed against the inserted CGI article and the specific DTA in force.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400,000,000 group consolidated turnover or balance-sheet total (CGI Article L. 13 AA) triggers mandatory full French TP documentation (Local File, Master File). A simplified TP documentation duty applies when cross-border related-party transactions exceed EUR 1,000,000 during the financial year. Country-by-Country reporting is separately required for groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 750,000,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not operate a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) statute in the Anglo-Gulf sense. However, the administration enforces substance through: (a) the permanent establishment attribution test under CGI Article 209(I); (b) abuse of law (abus de droit) under Article L. 64 LPF; and (c) beneficial ownership and substance requirements contained in French DTAs and the EU anti-tax-avoidance directives. A French SARL claiming treaty benefits, patent-box relief or EU Parent-Subsidiary exemption must demonstrate real premises, staff, business decisions, and risk management in France. A shell SARL without any operational substance will be denied the reduced DTA rates and CIT credits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting overseas consulting fees from the SARL's CIT return, issuing or using fictitious invoices, or creating artificial intercompany contracts designed to conceal taxable French-source profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CIT reassessment plus 80% penalty and late interest of 0.20% per month; criminal prosecution under CGI Article 1741 carries EUR 500,000 criminal fine and 5 years imprisonment; additional false-accounting sanctions under Article 1743 may impose EUR 500,000 fine and directors' disqualification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who signed fraudulent returns or orchestrated the concealment are jointly and severally liable under CGI Article 1750. Courts routinely impose personal asset forfeiture, 5-year directorship bans, travel bans and, in aggravated cases, immediate imprisonment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: SARL operated with no physical office, no employee, and no contractual business activity in France while claiming French CIT deductions, VAT refunds or DTA treaty benefits solely as a conduit for foreign funds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A sham company is recharacterised under the abuse-of-law procedure (Article L. 64 LPF), resulting in dismissal of all tax reliefs granted, repayment of claimed credits, and an abusive-tax-scheme penalty of 80% where the primary purpose is tax avoidance. Administrative fines for missing legal substance documents and failing to maintain registered office condition can reach EUR 50,000.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives who permitted the use of the corporate vehicle for abusive tax planning may be declared personally liable for unpaid taxes and interest under LPF Article L. 267. The French commercial court may also issue a déclaration de cessation des paiements, leading to an interdiction de gérer and personal travel ban.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving market-entry consultancy fees in cash or through unregulated channels above the EUR 10,000 cash-payment threshold, or conducting client transactions without the AML/KYC documentation required by the French Monetary and Financial Code for low-risk commercial activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: French AMF supervision under Code Monétaire et Financier Article L. 561-15 allows administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or 15% of the company's own funds for legal persons. Unreported foreign bank accounts trigger automatic taxation of undeclared assets plus a penalty equal to 12.5% of the undeclared account balance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Business owners face 5 years imprisonment and a EUR 375,000 fine for money-laundering offences under Article 324-1 of the Criminal Code. Directors may be placed under judicial control, have French bank accounts frozen, and be prohibited from conducting commercial activities during the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Charging excessive or under-invoiced management, licensing or consultancy fees between the French SARL and its non-resident shareholder without supporting OECD-compliant TP documentation, or failing to file the required French TP documentation after crossing statutory thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The tax administration may re-characterise transaction prices and reassess CIT; failure to produce TP documentation upon audit attracts a fixed penalty equal to 5% of the reassessed amount, compounded by the 40% bad-faith penalty and late interest of 0.20% per month. In a major cross-border manipulation, the CbC and Master File penalty is an additional EUR 20,000 per missing notification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who approved one-sided prices without an arm's-length benchmark can be held personally liable for the resulting corporate tax deficiency if the transaction is found to be an abuse of civil personality or company interest. Persistent TP violations trigger professional disqualification, seizure of personal assets, and a travel ban pending completion of the tax audit.
